reviews.review:
The game is entertaining, pretty much bug free, except stuttering problems during cinematics due to being ported from a console version, [strike](i heared limiting fps to 60 could fix it or lower said problem, it didn't do it or at least not for me)[/strike].
Full price? is an absolute outrage, for up to 20 bucks is super worth it IF you like it, if not 10~15 is more than fine given the mapping  and quality overall of the game, that being said, the story falls short specially in the last acts specially do to its length. So yeah, only on discount and i reccomend you fool at least another friendo to play with ya ocasionally.

I believe that the game has very good replayability due to how "encounters" and enemy modifiers are put into play or how it modifies the map a liiitle bit, conditions you enough for a second or third run of the game still feel quite fresh, and can be super challenging.

Completing the story doesn't take much honestly, the longer each map last around 1 Hour 10~30 mins and the others between 45 Mins or 1 Hour, it has 6 acts with their maps, except [spoiler]the 4th which just has 1 map[/spoiler] and if you just rush the story and intend to play just once the game... still enjoyable but you won't get everything in one run, if you look for that, this might not a game for you.

IF you like the game and/or have some friends that want to play, or even you might just plan in getting a game with all achievements in this game is more than comfortable to do so, nothing excessive and doesn't get repetitive or abusive as it gets in most L4D, or other games in general, and allows you experience other playstyles if you make the slight effort of making a buld which is super easy, or you just can copy someone else's build if u are not into it.

Getting all cards for builds ( using cards for skills is usually a concept i dislike and i did actually enjoyed in this game, took me close to 70 Hours, at 50 hours i had all but 5 or 6 that just increased ammo) requires no grinding, but a liittle bit of playing, offers pretty fine role playing specially when compared to games similar to L4D, i used to love those but now i would just play this and Zombie Army 4 because of the length of the game itself with DLCs and kinda because of the variety of playstyles they offer, in game is enough to feel the differences, it just suits me =)

Besides the currency used for the standard cards, there are the Skulls, which are obtained through certain maps which entry appears randomly, is not that they don't appear much, but it becomes something waay to expensive and grindy, you can buy consumable cards in Fort Hope that can have quite strong effects specially for the longer acts, doesn't really break the game, but in 225 hours i did not get all the custom stuff that appears there, that definately needs a re-design imo, u don't need them at all to get the achievements, complete the game in any difficulty nor they make the game better, u can even get some skins which i did get all... i think xD , i just had some banners left or smth, getting that currency is definately grindy, but not needed.

The game quality overall is pretty much... i dare say it would have been excellent if it were not for how poorly developed was at first, what a scam is the full price, and how suddenly the developling stopped after they tried to fix it up. I would like a workshop and a map designing option tho :3  The lenght and how in depth goes the story fell short for me, enjoyable but short, the rest of stuff was very enjoyable.

Visually is simply amazing, physics were mostly good, i had around 3 moments where bots where lauched into the air, and where clinging from... yes the air but i saw like they were completely on their toes holding onto a ledge, fun to see tho and u could rescue them... almost for sure, u had to be very unlucky not to be able to get them, a few orders to the bots, such us "mark a locked door so a bot uses their lockpick" worked around 2/3 of the time, won't use defibrilators sadly... also if they heal / shield you, they don't consume the item, and do it relatively often, compensates how much in the way they get XD

Now, i have to really MAKE THIS VERY CLEAR, the BOTs are good shooting, but SUCKS how much they cross or even stay in front of you instead of a liiitle bit behind you or through you, but not literally in front of where you are shooting... almost feels like they do it on purpose, really!   i had the luck to interiorice this but i WARN YOU it can be frustrating, dmg to them can be avoided with a card that nulifies the shooting/meele dmg u do or receive from others while you crouch, but they will still put their booteys in your ~face~ scope. Try to just ASSimilate and get a laugh or too with the comments they make when shot or when you shot someone, some were honestly pretty good x'D


 · A lot of ppl constantly compares this with [u]L4D2[/u] for obvious reasons... this goes for those of ya:

For me L4D2 fell quite behind over the years, and here goes a thing that many complained about, WORKSHOP!

Yes, the game doesn't have it, blame WB, screwing things up as usual btw, i just think of how MUCH i liked L4D2 when i used to play it, and i played it without workshop on console, years later i played it on pc with tons of workshop mods it was curious, the best is the fact that ppl made a few maps, but most of them were at best relatively decent and mostly half way done so lets be honest, besides the LED flashlight and a few other things, it just doesn't have that much of an impact, B4B could be improved via maps, sure, but agaiin lets be honest, ppl are just not going to put the work into it, and certainly not the quality, not remotely enough to compensate with the fact that the game was pretty much abandoned mid story, yes i said i liked it, but i also have to say, that the development had more than issues, specially since they released it almost exclusively designed for consoles, as prooves the FPS stuttering during cinematics that apparently only happen to PC players (look it up), when they were all kind of forced from one reason or another to abandon the game, now you know [i]W[/i]ho to [i]B[/i]lame.

So enough with L4D2 being that good, it WAS good! it is a good memory but as a game with years on it? it just fell behind. For example, i just played Titanfall 2 for the first time recently and holds its ground amazingly good, in general it aged super well!

Back 4 Blood is a good descendant, sadly it wasn't given the dedication it needed, and sure adding more content to it, a bit more to the story alongside and imo specially map related content and a few more enemy variants would definately improve it, and that being said, remains a good enjoyable game.

A modern clone of L4D2 featuring 4K intro and outro cutscenes. Each character comes with a unique special ability and a team bonus, so if you plan to play with friends, carefully choose your characters to ensure your team is well-balanced. Additionally, the selection of cards can further boost your team's strength. However, keep in mind that these are card-based mechanics, meaning only the top card in your deck will be active during each level. [i]Minor update[/i] I managed to built nice deck for one character according to Steam guides, however for single player on hard difficulties it gives nothing, [b]you only will have an advantage in online play with other your 3 friends if they have also one full deck for one character or full deck for each survivour[/b].

That said, the multiplayer community is totaly inactive. If you truly want to enjoy this game, it’s essential to gather three other friends who are also interested in playing. [b]Only under this condition should you consider purchasing the game[/b]. You can start a game with bots, but at any point, another player may join your session. Unfortunately, there is no option to kick players or create a private session with password protection. On the flip side, if you want to play with friends (two or three), you might assume that as the host, you can select a specific act or mission. However, it's possible to be added to another player’s game where only one person is playing, replacing the bots with you and your friends. That's why you need exactly 4 players. Keep in mind that only the host is required to own all DLCs. The game includes six acts, and you won’t find any community-made campaigns or levels, as these do not exist.
